chunks: Abu Sulayman Ahmad ibn Hawtha ibn Abu Hurasa al-Bahili narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq an-Nahawandi narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari narrated to us, from Sabah al-Muzni, from al-Harith ibn Hasira, from al-Asbagh ibn Nabata, from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) that he said:

Be like the bees among the birds; no bird is there but it considers them weak, but if the birds knew what blessing is in their interiors, they would not do that to them. Mix with people with your tongues and bodies, and separate from them with your hearts and deeds. And by He in whose hand is my soul, you will not see what you love until some of you spit in the faces of others, and some of you call others liars, and until none of you remains (or he said: from my Shias) except like the kohl in the eye and the salt in the food. And I will give you an example: it is like a man who had food, he sifted it and purified it, then he put it in a room and left it there as long as God willed, then he returned to it and found that it had been eaten by worms. He took it out, sifted it, purified it, and put it back in the room and left it there as long as God willed. Then he returned to it and found that a portion of it had been eaten by worms, so he took it out, sifted it, purified it, and put it back. He continued thus until only a bundle remained, like the bundle of the finest grain, which the worms could not harm at all. So too are you: you will be sifted/refined until only a small group remains, whom affliction will not harm at all.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the hadith comparing Shia to bees and the metaphor of sifting grain?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* articulates the doctrine of *al-Taqiyya* (dissimulation) as a strategic necessity for the Shia during the Minor and Major Ghaiba, emphasizing outward conformity to avoid persecution while maintaining inner fidelity. The metaphor of the bee illustrates how the community’s perceived weakness masks divine blessing, while the analogy of grain purified from weevils signifies the gradual sifting of the faithful through tribulations until only a resilient, pure core remains. This narrative underscores the historical reality of Shia minority status and the scholarly emphasis on spiritual resilience amidst social integration.
